how_scored: Same or more = 0; a bit less = 50; much less or dries at times = 100
why: The direct sign of decline, which is what vulnerability means in this project. Daniel et al. 2021 impact group. Weight cut from 20 to 10 (Rajat, 23 Oct 2026): it is people's recall, so the measured flow indicators now carry more.

how_scored: 5 L/min or more = 0; 1-5 = 50; under 1 or dries = 100 (field form bands)
why: A small dry-season flow has little margin left. SOP ch. 5; ICIMOD 2018. Weight raised from 7 to 10 (Rajat, 23 Oct 2026).

A big swing means a small or shallow store that empties fast after the rains. SOP ch. 5; Dass et al. 2026. Weight cut from 6 to 3 (16 Oct 2026) because lean flow already counts in two other indicators.

indicator: Months with low or no flow
needs: field (month calendar: low months, and months with no flow at all)
how_scored: Low-flow months: 0 = 0; 1 = 25; 2-3 = 50; 4 or more = 100. Any month with no flow at all scores at least 75 (3 or more dry months = 100), whatever the low-flow count.
why: Long lean periods leave users short for much of the year. Spring Atlas; SOP. Weight 13 and the dry-month floor (Rajat, 23 Oct 2026): even one month with no flow is a strong sign of vulnerability, so it never scores 0.

how_scored: No issue = 0; muddy after rain = 50; contamination or illness = 100
why: Muddy after rain points to shallow, fast flow paths that are easily disturbed.

how_scored: Perennial = 0; seasonal-perennial = 25; seasonal = 50; highly seasonal or ephemeral = 100
why: Kept minor on purpose: a spring that has always been seasonal is not declining; only a change in seasonality is.

indicator: Households per L/min of lean flow (pressure on users)
why: Many users on a small flow is the main human pressure. It measures pressure on the people who use the spring, not decline itself. SOP ch. 5; Resource Book.

how_scored: Fewer or same = 0; more = 50; much more = 100
why: More households, tourists or piped schemes drawing on the same spring raise demand while supply may not grow. Field form: "more users" as a reason for change.

how_scored: None = 0; one = 50; two or more, or a latrine/soak pit = 100
why: Threatens use of the water even if flow holds. SOP ch. 4.

how_scored: Little = 0; some = 50; major = 100
why: Cuts infiltration in the likely recharge area. Daniel 2021; SOP.

indicator: Area prone to landslides, cloudbursts or flash floods
how_scored: No = 0; minor events = 50; major events in the last 10 years = 100
why: Landslides and flash floods bury outlets, cut pipelines and change the slope that feeds the spring. Asked of users (Rajat, 23 Oct 2026) and read with the GSI landslide map (separate indicator).

how_scored: Percentile among the input springs: less rain = higher score
why: Winter and pre-monsoon rain feeds the spring in the months it is lowest. Daniel 2021 rainfall stressor.

how_scored: Percentile among the input springs: drier = higher score
why: Less water left over for recharge after evaporation.

how_scored: Percentile among the input springs: faster drying = higher score
why: Falling rain means less recharge year after year: the rainfall stressor of Daniel et al. 2021. Trend over 24 IMD years (2012 missing); at most cells it is not statistically certain, so read it as a direction.

how_scored: Percentile among the input springs: more variable = higher score
why: Dry years hit harder where rain swings a lot from year to year. 24 years of IMD data. Weight cut by 1 (23 Oct 2026) to make room for shallow soil and mapped landslides.

how_scored: Percentile among the input springs: faster growth = higher score
why: Stand-in for population growth: more houses mean more users and more sealed ground near the spring. Model estimates from yearly imagery, so small changes are noise. Weight cut by 1 (23 Oct 2026) to make room for shallow soil and mapped landslides.

indicator: Built-up, cropland and bare land within 500 m
how_scored: Percentile among the input springs: more disturbed land = higher score
why: Less forest and more sealed or tilled land means less infiltration near the spring. Stand-in until Module B maps the real recharge zone. Weight cut by 1 (23 Oct 2026) to make room for shallow soil and mapped landslides.

how_scored: Percentile among the input springs: steeper = higher score
why: Steep slopes shed rain as runoff before it can soak in. Weight cut by 1 (23 Oct 2026) to make room for shallow soil and mapped landslides.

indicator: Land rising above the spring within 1 km
how_scored: Percentile among the input springs: less rise = higher score
why: A spring close to a ridge top has little land above it to collect recharge. Weight cut by 1 (23 Oct 2026) to make room for shallow soil and mapped landslides.

how_scored: Percentile among the input springs: shallower soil = higher score
why: Thin soil stores little rain, so less is left to feed the spring in the dry months. SoilGrids caps depth at 200 cm, so deep soils tie. Model estimate, not a pit.

how_scored: None within 500 m = 0; one or more within 500 m = 50; spring inside or within 100 m of one = 100
why: A mapped slide close to the spring means unstable ground that can bury the outlet or reroute the water. Read with the field question on disasters.

how_scored: Both = 0; one = 50; neither = 100
why: Protected, managed springs are looked after when problems start. Resource Book; SOP ch. 6.

needs: field (which works: check dams, trenches, pits, ponds, plantation, DI; and their condition)
how_scored: Present and maintained = 0; present but neglected = 50; none = 100
why: Trenches, pits and plantation uphill raise recharge (Mathamali: 5.7 to 19.5 L/min). Daniel 2021.
